query: What are the approved therapies for Spinal Muscular Atrophy mentioned in the guidelines?
ground_truth_answer: The three FDA-approved disease-modifying therapies for Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA) are: 1) Nusinersen (Spinraza), an intrathecal antisense oligonucleotide; 2) Onasemnogene abeparvovec (Zolgensma), an AAV9-based IV gene replacement therapy; and 3) Risdiplam (Evrysdi), an oral small-molecule SMN2 pre-mRNA splicing modifier.

query: Why can SMN1 deletions be missed in short-read sequencing?
ground_truth_answer: SMN1 and SMN2 share high sequence identity (differing by only a single nucleotide in exon 7). Short-read sequencing struggles to uniquely map reads in this repetitive and duplicated region, leading to missed diagnoses unless specialized caller tools or long-read sequencing are used.

query: What are the advantages of long-read sequencing in detecting chromosomal rearrangements?
ground_truth_answer: Long-read sequencing (such as PacBio HiFi and Oxford Nanopore) spans repetitive regions, complex breakpoints, and structural variations that are invisible to short reads, allowing base-pair resolution of balanced translocations, inversions, and complex insertions.
